summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier proprietary families — OpenAI's GPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude — which together capture the majority of consumer traffic and enterprise API spend. Open-weight models led by Meta's Llama, Alibaba's Qwen, and DeepSeek have achieved near-frontier performance and drive massive HuggingFace download volumes and self-hosted deployments. Crucially, real-world enterprise adoption increasingly flows through cloud aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), which amplifies the reach of models available across multiple platforms well beyond their direct-API numbers.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-4o (GPT series)
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT held ~54-55% of worldwide AI chatbot web traffic in 2026 and GPT leads OpenRouter and developer surveys; available via direct API and Azure OpenAI, giving it enormous enterprise reach.
models.best_for: General-purpose reasoning, agents, and production applications requiring reliability

models.name: Gemini 2.5 / 3.1 Pro (Gemini series)
models.popularity_notes: Gemini's web visits grew ~450% YoY to 2.9B monthly visits and hold ~26-28% chatbot share; native availability on Google Vertex AI drives deep enterprise adoption.
models.best_for: Long-context document processing and Google Cloud-native enterprise deployments

models.name: Claude Opus / Sonnet (Claude series)
models.popularity_notes: Menlo Ventures put Anthropic at ~40% of enterprise API usage (highest share), with Claude web visits up ~855% YoY; available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex for broad enterprise reach.
models.best_for: Enterprise coding assistants and safety-critical agentic workflows

models.name: Llama 4 (Llama series)
models.popularity_notes: The most-downloaded open-weight family on HuggingFace and the default self-hosted choice; available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx — the widest aggregator footprint of any open model.
models.best_for: Self-hosted, on-premise, and customizable enterprise deployments

models.name: Qwen3 (Qwen series)
models.popularity_notes: Adopted by over 90,000 enterprises and a top HuggingFace download leader; redefined open-weights with 1T+ parameter variants and strong multilingual/coding performance.
models.best_for: Multilingual applications and cost-sensitive open-weight deployments

models.name: DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 (DeepSeek series)
models.popularity_notes: Held ~4% of chatbot web traffic and remains a top OpenRouter model; MIT-licensed open weights with frontier-level reasoning at dramatically lower training/serving cost drive heavy developer adoption.
models.best_for: High-volume reasoning and coding workloads on a budget

models.name: Mistral Large / Mixtral (Mistral series)
models.popularity_notes: A leading European open-weight provider available on AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex; valued for speed, efficiency, and data-sovereignty-friendly deployment.

models.name: Grok-4 (Grok series)
models.popularity_notes: Grok held ~2.4% of chatbot web traffic (up YoY) with deep integration into the X platform providing real-time data and a large captive user base.
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval and consumer-facing chat applications

models.name: Phi-4 (Phi series)
models.popularity_notes: A top small-model download on HuggingFace and natively promoted through Azure AI, favored for high-performance reasoning in small-scale and edge deployments.
models.best_for: Edge, on-device, and cost-constrained reasoning tasks

models.name: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-powered)
models.popularity_notes: Held ~1.3% of chatbot web traffic and reaches hundreds of millions of enterprise seats via Microsoft 365 and Azure, making it a major enterprise AI consumption channel.
models.best_for: Enterprise productivity within the Microsoft ecosystem

models.name: Command R+ (Command series)
models.popularity_notes: Enterprise-focused model available on AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, and Oracle Cloud, with adoption clustering near the lower tier through its RAG/retrieval specialization.
models.best_for: Enterprise retrieval-augmented generation and search applications
